brief: Last Thursday's correlated selloff (Nasdaq 100 broke 4.8% below its 200DMA, Philly semis fell 12% on the week, the S&P had its worst week since April 2025, and the NYSE printed its first 80% downside-volume day in nearly a year) gave way today to a broad, low-volume bounce (S&P +2.5%, Nasdaq 100 +3.5%, SOX +5% despite Nvidia -6% on Jensen Huang's spy scandal, VIX down over 5 points to 20). BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky says history (15 prior first-time 80%-downside-days since 1996) puts the odds of another one within 30 days at roughly 73%, with 20-day forward SPX returns a coin-toss: not yet a "fat pitch." He wants SPX closer to 7,000-7,100 (breadth under 30% above 200DMA, versus 58% now) before turning bullish. Goldman's desk agrees the bounce reflects a lack of supply, not real buying, with CTAs still net sellers and roughly $25bn more supply modeled this week. Semis carry six months of underwater overhead supply; Krinsky's SOX retrace target is 8,000-8,300. He flags healthcare (XLV) and Apple as vulnerable "hideouts." JPMorgan's Lakos-Bujas (8,000 SPX year-end target) and Morgan Stanley's Wilson see the correction as nearly over.
